evidence: Revenue acceleration is dramatic.

Traders should treat the forward EPS of $15.72 as the key hurdle — evidence of continued sequential revenue growth and gross-margin defense above 53% is required to justify the multiple.

But here's the thing — none of those are reasons to sell a stock that just posted +50% YoY revenue growth, swung operating income from negative to nearly $2 billion, and is riding the single most powerful secular demand wave in modern tech.
Meanwhile, the fundamentals report has hard, verified numbers: revenue acceleration, margin expansion, operating leverage, net cash, capex ramp.
The bull case rests on verified revenue growth of +50% YoY, gross margin expansion of 1,400 bps, operating income swinging $2.1B positive, and a fortress balance sheet.

The bear's sharpest sub-point — receivables up +20.6% QoQ [fragmentid: srcd889dd1e36a5d55a:frag:0] against revenue growth of +12.5%, i.e., receivables growing faster than revenue — is a legitimate early-warning flag that the bull did not address.

He cites receivables growing +20.6% QoQ [fragmentid: srcd889dd1e36a5d55a:frag:0] against +12.5% revenue growth as a warning sign, and free cash flow falling to $1,558M from $2,566M sequentially [fragmentid: src4045667791b919f9:frag:0] on a $808M capex step-up and a $730M working-capital drag.

The neutral analyst's three adjustments are the right ones: nudge the trim from one-third to about 40%, place the stop at roughly 610 rather than exactly at the 10 EMA at 618.52 [fragmentid: src388228ad9e12e09d:frag:0] where it is the most obvious stop-run level on the chart, and treat the conservative analyst's additional re-entry conditions (receivables growth decelerating back toward revenue growth, free cash flow recovering as capex normalizes) as confirmatory rather than disqualifying.
